title: 90-161.Z for wing PFMs: what it takes to install and run

slides.title: 90-161.Z for wing PFMs: what it takes to install and run
slides.subtitle:
For a Publications and Forms Manager deciding whether to install it at their wing
Draft r6 · 13 November 2026
slides.notes: Audience: a wing PFM. Covers what it does, what you need, setup, updates, upkeep, limits, approvals and risks.

slides.title: What you get, and what it asks of you

cards.label: stages of DAFMAN 90-161 tracked per action, from appointment of the action officer to the 4-year review
to set up: a rights check, the lists, the app and flows, then a first-run setup screen
new licenses expected: standard DoD365 tools only (confirm with your license manager)

list: It is not approved for use yet: your wing needs the reviews on slide 13.
Setup checks your rights first and tells you what to ask for; every right has a fallback.
It needs a little upkeep each month and a handover plan before you move (slide 11).

slides.title: One tracked path from request to posted publication
slides.lead: One record per action; coordination routed and tracked; format applied by code; every event logged.
slides.key: Stages 0-12 per DAFMAN 90-161 (legal last: 3.4, 5.1.8.2). Yellow: code, not people, applies the DAFMAN format and checks each format rule.

cards.head: Action officers
cards.body: Request an action, upload drafts, name coordinators, see status at any time.

cards.head: Coordinators and officials
cards.body: Get the request with a due date and reminders; answer Concur, Concur with comment, Nonconcur or No comment.

cards.head: You, the PFM
cards.body: One queue: format and check drafts, post, keep the product index, run periodic reviews.

slides.title: Built only on what every wing already has
inside: 9 lists today, 3 more approved: actions, coordination, product index, reviews, settings, activity log
Routing, weekday reminders, escalation, stage gates, review timers
Intake, status, PFM queue, first-run setup, settings, update check
PowerShell and Word build the DAFMAN format and check every rule
Extracts the draft's words as data; it never sets format
Tells your app that a new version exists
outside: Design, code and fake sample data; you download the packages from it
Used by the maintainer for design with fake data only
Step-by-step tasks for the gov computer

slides.title: For and against, for your wing
pros: Every action and its status in one place; customers see their own status
DAFMAN format and rules enforced by code, not memory
Weekday reminders and escalation without chasing by hand
Works with a site owner's rights; each extra right has a fallback
Updates announced in the app; most updates are data copies
cons: Not approved for use yet; your wing needs its own reviews
Built and supported by one maintainer today
Needs setup time and a backup person
SharePoint and Power Apps limits apply (slide 12)
Coordinators outside the wing work by e-mail, not in the app
The formatter needs Word and PowerShell on a gov computer

slides.rule: Design rule: every rule that can change lives in list rows, so most updates are data copies, not re-imports.
